gallery.filename: A Yancey County student collects stream insects (9897361693).jpg
gallery.title: File:A Yancey County student collects stream insects (9897361693).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Southeast Region
gallery.description:
Each year the Toes in the Toe Watershed Discovery event brings 5th-grade students from North Carolina’s Yancey and Mitchell counties out to a river in their community. On the banks of the river they rotate through a variety of educational stations focused on stream health and the importance of river. Stations include art, farming, energy, fish, and stream macroinvertebrates.
Because the watershed is home to the endangered Appalachian elktoe mussel, the Fish & Wildlife Service helped create the event and continues to help students explore the North and South Toe rivers in search of stream insects, mollusks, and other animals.

Photo credit: Gary Peeples/USFWS

gallery.filename: Yancey County student gets a closer look at the river (8019706322).jpg
gallery.title: File:Yancey County student gets a closer look at the river (8019706322).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Southeast Region
gallery.description:
Each year, the Toes in the Toe Discovery program brings nearly every 5th grade student in North Carolina’s Yancey and Mitchell counties out to a river in their community - Mitchell County students visit the North Toe River, while Yancey County students visit the South Toe River. The students rotate through a number of stations, including collecting stream invertebrates, discussing watershed health, and exploring rivers through art. Organized by the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service and Toe River Valley Watch, the event draws the support of many community partners, including RiverLink, the N.C. Division of Water Quality, N.C. Natural Heritage Program, Sundance Solar, Penland School of Crafts, N.C. Cooperative Extension, the Blue Ridge Resource Conservation and Development Commission, Mountain Heritage High School, Mitchell County High School, Tri-County Christian School, Yancey County, Mitchell County, and many community volunteers.



Photo Credit: Gary Peeples/USFWS
